outcome: The conjecture was proved for all sufficiently large n by Kang, Kelly, Kühn, Methuku, and Osthus (arXiv preprint January 2021, published in Annals of Mathematics in 2023) — entirely before the frozen revision's date. No mathematical progress on the conjecture (for the remaining finite range of small n, or otherwise) has appeared in the 26 January 2024 – present window; the only post-window item is a March 2025 expository/historical Mathematics Magazine article recounting the problem's fifty-year history and the 2021/2023 proof, which reports no new results.
summary: The Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture (chromatic index of a linear hypergraph on n vertices is at most n) was resolved for all sufficiently large n by Kang, Kelly, Kühn, Methuku and Osthus: preprint arXiv:2101.04698 posted January 2021, published in the Annals of Mathematics in 2023 (https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2023/198-2/p02). Both events are well before the frozen revision's date of 26 January 2024, so this is classified open_stale — a case the source list had already been settled by when the snapshot was taken, and the list simply had not been updated. I searched extensively for anything in the 2024-2026 window: general searches for new proofs or progress, searches for computational/SAT-solver work on the remaining small cases (n<12, since Hindman/others had verified n≤10 and later n≤12 computationally, and a 2023 Dagstuhl paper 'A SAT Solver's Opinion on the Erdős-Faber-Lovász Conjecture' used SAT Modulo Symmetries to probe small non-colorable hypergraphs), and searches specifically for AI/LLM involvement. The only item found dated after the frozen revision is 'The Erdős-Faber-Lovász Conjecture: Fifty Exciting Years' (Mathematics Magazine, accepted January 2024, published online March 2025, https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/0025570X.2024.2419818) — this is an expository/historical retrospective on the conjecture's fifty-year history and the 2021/2023 proof, not a report of new mathematical results (the paywalled full text could not be fetched directly — HTTP 403 — but its abstract, framing across multiple listings, and the fact that no other source treats it as new progress make this clear). I also fetched the current Wikipedia article, which states only that the conjecture 'was resolved for all sufficiently large n' in 2023 and makes no mention of AI, computer assistance, SAT solvers, or remaining open small cases. No source anywhere associates any AI system with this conjecture at any point, before or after the window; the ai_role is therefore 'none' with no basis quote available, as required when no authors' account exists to cite.
competing_reading: None of substance. One could argue the 2023 SAT-solver paper on remaining small non-colorable hypergraphs (a computer-assisted, not AI, method) might have had a post-window follow-up narrowing the finite exceptional range further, but no such follow-up was found in any search, and even if one existed a SAT solver is explicitly excluded from the AI codes under §6.2.
what_would_settle_it: A dedicated search of arXiv's math.CO listing for 2024-2026 papers citing arXiv:2101.04698 or explicitly addressing the small remaining cases of Erdős-Faber-Lovász, or full access to the paywalled 'Fifty Exciting Years' article, would close out any residual doubt, but nothing in the searches performed suggests such a paper exists.
